references.text: Describes the garden of Eden that God planted, similar to the comparison in Gen 13:10 where the Jordan Valley is described as 'the Lord's garden' (כְּגַן־יְהוָה).
The fulfillment of what Gen 13:10 foretells: 'before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.' This verse describes the actual destruction.
Uses the same expression 'like the garden of Eden' (כְּגַן־יְהוָה) regarding Zion's restoration, a direct parallel to the description of the Jordan Valley in Gen 13:10.
Zoar (צוער) is mentioned as the city Lot fled to, the same place noted in Gen 13:10 as a boundary marker for the fertile area: 'on the way to Zoar.'
Mentions God's garden (Eden), a parallel to the expression 'the Lord's garden' used for the Jordan Valley in Gen 13:10.
Egypt's fertility is known from Abraham and Sarah's stay there, relevant to the comparison 'like the land of Egypt' (כְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם) in Gen 13:10.
The verses form a narrative and theological framework around Lot's flight, where Zoar shifts from being a viewpoint in a time of abundance to becoming the place of refuge during judgment.
